notes: Two separate circuits are built: the sender (mkr1, bb1, btn1) and the receiver (mkr2, bb2, led1, r1). Each board has its own antenna.

The antenna type antenna-gps-active-sma comes from the parts list. I could not check its ports, so the antenna edges leave the antenna port null and use the board's ANT port, the u.FL connector. The ANT port belongs to the new MKR WAN 1310 type.

The breadboard catalogue calls bank 't' rows a-e, but the images label the top half f-j. I mapped image rows j,i,h,g,f to catalogue rows a,b,c,d,e on bank 't'. The part legs are in image row g (catalogue d), and the jumper ends are in image row f (catalogue e).

Image columns were read from pixel positions. The pushbutton legs are in columns 5 and 7 and the black and yellow wires share those columns. The pushbutton's two sides are assumed to be 1.l and 2.r, because the image shows only two legs, one on each side.
The pushbutton has no external resistor. The sketch uses INPUT_PULLUP, so the button pulls pin 2 to GND when pressed.

In the receiver, the LED cathode (shorter lead) is in column 6 with the GND wire. The anode (bent, longer lead) is in column 8 with the resistor. The resistor runs from column 8 to column 11, where the green wire from pin 2 ends.
The resistor value is not given in the manual, so I assumed 220 ohms, a typical LED series resistor.
The USB cables and the laptop are not modelled, because the diagrams do not show them.
